name: Shah Jamnadas C. Ghariwala
why_it_matters: Founded 9 July 1899 — 126 years old, in the middle of Chauta Bazaar, still run by the third, fourth and fifth generations. Ghari (mawa + ghee + sugar disc, often pista- or kesar-filled) is Surat's signature sweet, eaten in massive quantities on Chandni Padvo (the festival night after Sharad Purnima). Jamnadas is the city's reference ghari maker; the recipe pre-dates the brand.
insider_tip: Buy ghari the day you'll eat it — it's mawa-based and only keeps 5 days. Pista is the order most regulars get; mawa-plain is the under-rated old-school one. Avoid the imitator shops on the same street (there are 6+ 'Jamnadas' variants); the original is the corner shop with the original board.
signature_address: Lalubhai Sheth Street, Chauta Bazaar, Surat, Gujarat 395003

name: Sasumaa Gujarati Thali
why_it_matters: Established 1999 — 26 years of unlimited Gujarati thali in Athwa, the city's restaurant district. Tripadvisor 4.0, in Surat top 20. Surti thali is its own dialect (sweeter, more coconut, lighter on chilli than Kathiyawadi); Sasumaa is the place out-of-towners default to for it. Branded with the Gujarati 'mother-in-law' nostalgia hook.
insider_tip: Winter (Nov-Feb) is the season — that's when ponkh (fresh sorghum) and undhiyu show up on the thali. Lunch (12-3pm) is the move; dinner repeats the same dishes but the curries are reheated. Refills are unlimited but ask once before they stop circulating.
signature_address: Parle Point, City Light Road, Athwa, Surat, Gujarat 395007

name: Jani Farsan House
why_it_matters: Locho is Surat's accidental dish — a botched khaman that congealed into something better, half-set gram-flour with masala, oil, sev, onions, lemon. Jani Farsan is one of the city's three reference locho stalls (with Gopal and Ram). Tripadvisor 4.2; the texture of the locho here is firmer than Gopal's, looser than Ram's — the middle path.
insider_tip: Locho only stays 2 hours — eat it warm, off the iron pan; takeaway loses 30% of the texture. Order with extra oil and lemon; default servings hold back. The sev khamani upgrade is the second-best dish; the khandvi is plated, not rolled — different from the Ahmedabad cut.
signature_address: Parle Point Junction, City Light Road, Athwa, Surat, Gujarat 395007

name: Gopal Locho
why_it_matters: Gopal Locho is the softer-style locho — looser texture than Jani's, generally considered the city's reference for first-timers. Parle Point junction location is the original; multiple newer outlets exist around Surat. Locho with sev and the dab of butter on top is the Surat morning order that's been the same for 50+ years.
insider_tip: Mornings (8-11am) for the first batch — by afternoon the locho is reheated. Take it on the steel plate they serve it on at the stall, eat standing; takeaway containers ruin the texture in 10 minutes. The sev khamani box for the train ride is the local move.
signature_address: Parle Point Junction, Athwa, Surat, Gujarat 395007

name: The Lime Tree
why_it_matters: Rooftop restaurant at Lords Plaza on Athwa — Tripadvisor 4.8, ranked #7 of 600+ restaurants in Surat. Fairy-lit terrace ambience that pulls the city's date-night and special-occasion bookings. Better at the tandoor than the multi-cuisine pretensions of newer rivals.
insider_tip: Book the terrace seating, not the indoor — the AC indoor side is a different (worse) experience. Best between October and March; April-June nights are too humid for rooftop dining. The mixed tandoor platter for two is the order; the sizzlers are second tier.
signature_address: Rooftop, Lords Plaza, Athwa Gate, Athwa, Surat, Gujarat 395001

name: Pavilion
signature_dish: Pizza and pasta with city skyline view
why_it_matters: Vesu's high-rise restaurant district anchor — Tripadvisor 4.9, top-5 Surat dining. Skyline views over the city's newest residential belt. The pizza-pasta game is sharper than at most Indian fine-dining; sourcing through Mumbai. Wins for occasion dining where you want a non-Indian palette and city-light view.
insider_tip: Reservation only — they don't entertain walk-ins on weekends. Window seats are first-come; ask explicitly when booking. The wood-fired margherita is the test pie and it passes. The sizzlers (Indian-style) are weaker than the Italian section; choose the kitchen's lane.
signature_address: Top Floor, Lalbhai Contractor Stadium Road, Vesu, Surat, Gujarat 395007

name: Surat Baking Company (SBC)
why_it_matters: SBC is Surat's reference bakery-café — Tripadvisor 4.9, top-3 ranked. Floor-to-ceiling glass on Ghod Dod Road, the city's most fashionable food street. Bakes fresh on premises; sourdough was a city-first when they opened. The kitchen handles pizzas, sandwiches and full meals — not a coffee-only stop.
insider_tip: Get there before 11am if you want the cinnamon rolls; they sell out by lunch. The margherita pizza is on the under-cooked side by design; ask for 'extra-baked' if you want crisper. Skip the pasta — it's the weakest section of the menu.
signature_address: Ground Floor, Ghod Dod Road, Athwa, Surat, Gujarat 395007

name: Spice Terrace
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor 5.0 — top-ranked Surat restaurant on the platform. Adajan side draws the Surati family/extended-family dinner crowd; the live folk music sets are a draw most rival venues don't have. Multi-cuisine but it's the tandoor and dal-makhani section that does the heavy lifting.
insider_tip: Folk music nights are usually Friday-Sunday — confirm when booking. Sit on the open terrace; the indoor section misses the whole point. The paneer tikka is the order; biryani is mid-tier here.
signature_address: L.P. Savani Road, Adajan, Surat, Gujarat 395009

name: Dotivala Bakery
why_it_matters: Dotivala is the bakery that invented nankhatai — Faramji Pestonji Dotivala began baking it in the 1850s as a response to the Dutch leaving Surat (the Dutch had taught his predecessors to make leavened bread; without yeast, he reformulated). 175 years of continuous run, still family-operated in Nanpura. India's oldest commercial bakery on most counts.
insider_tip: Buy the original (plain) nankhatai, not the flavoured variants — the recipe is what's historic; the elaichi/almond add-ons are 2000s additions. Mawa cake is the second must-buy. Ask for the wax-paper packet, not the plastic — they still pack the traditional way if you request it.

name: Vintage Asia
why_it_matters: The city's reference pan-Asian restaurant — Tripadvisor 4.9, top-5. Sushi and tempura on a menu that genuinely separates Chinese/Japanese/Thai rather than blurring them into Indo-Chinese. Wins for the date-night Surati who wants something the city's wedding-banquet pan-Asians don't deliver.
insider_tip: Order from the Thai section if you want the kitchen's strongest dishes — the green curry and khao suey are noticeably better executed than the sushi side. Sushi is veg-only at most outlets; calibrate expectations. Reservations on weekends are mandatory.
